_meta.description: Master performance standards library — all breeds, all species (comprehensive)
_meta.age_unit_note: Broilers/turkey/duck/quail meat use 'day'; layers/breeders/turkey breeders/goose use 'week'

_meta.source: American Boer Goat Association (ABGA) performance records; Ohio State University Extension; peer-reviewed literature (Pinkerton et al. 1991; Lu & Potchoiba 1988). Official breed standard data.
_meta.note: ADG under feedlot: 150–200 g/day. Extensive: 130–150 g/day.

pre_wean.label: Boer – Pre-wean Kid (0–8 weeks, birth–15 kg)
pre_wean.note: Dam-raised; suckling + creep feed from week 2.

grower.label: Boer – Growing Kid (8–20 weeks, 15–33 kg)
grower.note: Fastest ADG phase. Feedlot: 150–200 g/day. Extensive: 130–150 g/day.

finisher.label: Boer – Finishing Kid (20–32 weeks, 33–50 kg)
finisher.note: Market weight target 35–45 kg (6–8 months for quality cabrito; 40–50 kg for carcass market).

_meta.source: New Zealand Kiko Goat Association; American Kiko Goat Association records; Pinkerton et al. extension literature (estimated from field data).
_meta.note: Hardy low-input breed. Slower growth than Boer but excellent parasite resistance. Developed in NZ from feral does x Nubian/Toggenburg/Saanen.

_meta.source: Langston University E. (Kika) de la Garza Institute for Goat Research; USDA AMS records (estimated). NRC 2007.
_meta.note: Feral origin US breed. Hardy, lean, good forager. Slower growth, very low input costs.

pre_wean.label: Spanish Goat Kid – Pre-wean (0–8 weeks, birth–10 kg)
pre_wean.note: Suckling; creep feed optional. Very low-input early growth.

grower.label: Spanish Goat Kid – Grower (8–20 weeks, 10–20 kg)
grower.note: Moderate ADG typical of hardy range breed. Superior foraging reduces supplemental feed costs.

finisher.label: Spanish Goat Kid – Finisher/Growing Meat (20–36 weeks, 20–32 kg)
finisher.note: Slower finishing than Boer. Market weight 25–30 kg at 28–36 weeks depending on management.

_meta.source: South African Kalahari Red Goat Breeders Society; peer-reviewed South African production data (estimated weekly curve from breed summary).
_meta.note: South African meat breed similar to Boer but all-red. Excellent heat tolerance, slightly heavier frame.

_meta.source: South African Savanna Goat Breeders Society; extension literature (estimated from breed standard data).
_meta.note: White South African meat breed. Heat tolerant, good mothering. Performance slightly below Boer.

_meta.source: Myotonic Goat Registry; Tennessee State University Extension (estimated from field data).
_meta.note: Fainting/Tennessee Stiff-Leg goat. High muscle-to-bone ratio, excellent carcass quality. Slow growth.

_meta.source: BLRI Bangladesh Livestock Research Institute + FAO. Birth 1.1 kg, 3-month 5.5 kg, 6-month 9 kg, yearling 13 kg. Highly prolific 1.9 kids/birth. Superior glazed leather.
USDA AMS Dairy Goat National Genetic Evaluation; French INRAE breed reference (994 kg/305d); University of Georgia Extension Dairy Goat Production guide; ScienceDirect Saanen overview.
_meta.note: World's highest-producing dairy goat. White coat. Peak milk 5.7 L/day average, up to 11.3 L/day in top does.

_meta.source: USDA AMS Dairy Goat National Genetic Evaluation; University of Georgia Extension; French Alpine breed references (933 kg/307d INRAE).
_meta.note: Second highest-producing dairy goat. Multi-colored coat. Good adaptability.

_meta.source: USDA AMS Dairy Goat National Genetic Evaluation; University of Georgia Extension (1820 lbs/lactation = 825 kg); Anglo-Nubian breed society UK.
_meta.note: Lower volume but highest fat and protein of all dairy breeds. Long drooping ears. Popular in tropics.

_meta.source: USDA AMS Dairy Goat National Genetic Evaluation; University of Georgia Extension (2115 lbs = 960 kg / lactation); Swiss Toggenburg breed society.
_meta.note: Oldest known dairy goat breed. Brown with white markings. Consistent producer, good in cooler climates.

_meta.source: USDA AMS Dairy Goat National Genetic Evaluation; University of Georgia Extension (2100 lbs = 953 kg / lactation); American LaMancha Club.
_meta.note: Distinctive very small ears. High butterfat. Heat tolerant. Developed in the US.

_meta.source: USDA AMS Dairy Goat National Genetic Evaluation; University of Georgia Extension (2146 lbs = 974 kg / lactation).
_meta.note: Bay-colored Swiss breed. Sweet mild milk. Less common than Saanen/Alpine but excellent quality.

_meta.source: LPRI Pakistan + GoatJournal breed profile. 1.0-3.0 L/day avg 1.8 L for 150-170 days (avg 161 days). Fat 5%, Protein 3.5%.
Pakistan Livestock Research; Punjab Agriculture University; FAO Domestic Animal Diversity breed data (estimated from published field data).
_meta.note: Widely used dual-purpose breed in South Asia. Good meat and moderate milk. Large body with curved horns.

_meta.source: Central Institute for Research on Goats (CIRG), India; FAO breed data (estimated from published records).
_meta.note: Small compact dual-purpose breed. High prolificacy (twins/triplets common). Popular in India for both meat and milk.

_meta.source: South African Angora Stud Breeders Society; Texas A&M AgriLife Extension; American Angora Goat Breeders Association (estimated from published data).
_meta.note: Produces lustrous mohair fiber. Shorn twice yearly. More delicate than meat breeds, sensitive to cold/wet.

_meta.source: FAO Animal Production and Health guidelines; Inner Mongolia Agricultural University data; Australian Cashmere Goat Society (estimated).
_meta.note: Cashmere is the fine undercoat, combed/dehaired annually. Body weight varies widely by region. Performance highly variable.
